name: Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā al-Lakhmī al-Gharnāṭī al-Shāṭibī
summary: Mālikī jurist of Granada, famed for al-Muwāfaqāt on the aims of the law, who also wrote al-Maqāṣid al-shāfiya, one of the largest commentaries on the Alfiyya.
bio: Al-Shāṭibī lived and taught in Granada, the last Muslim kingdom of al-Andalus, and is known above all for his books on the principles and aims of the law, al-Muwāfaqāt and al-Iʿtiṣām.

He was a grammarian too: his al-Maqāṣid al-shāfiya fī sharḥ al-Khulāṣa al-kāfiya comments on the Alfiyya verse by verse at great length, with a jurist's care for definitions and evidence, and is printed in ten volumes. He died in Granada in 790/1388. He is not the Qurʾān reader al-Shāṭibī, author of the poem on the seven readings.

works.title: al-Maqāṣid al-shāfiya fī sharḥ al-Khulāṣa al-kāfiya
